conviction_note: Baseline median reaction of 3.73% is unusable (its own event_plausibility verdict is cadence_implausible - the eight 'prints' are 6-Ks eight days apart, not earnings), and 20-day realised vol is 114.6%; I take a sizeable negative because two pre-print company filings stack a share-and-warrant-funded pivot acquisition on top of a 1-for-10 reverse split effective the day after the print, and the 182.7m-share blow-off that greeted the pivot had fully faded before the release.

findings.finding: On the evening of 2026-09-01, hours before this before-the-open print, CollPlant announced a 1-for-10 reverse share split to take effect at the Nasdaq open on 2026-09-04 - the session immediately AFTER the print - explicitly 'as part of the Company's strategic plan to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement for continued listing'.
findings.corpus_ref: docs/ee32750e276846aba37596bed7e3b23135338ee9.txt (snapshots/20260902T150801Z.json item 1); the underlying filing is filings.json/snapshot accession 0001213900-26-096233, form 6-K accepted 2026-09-01T20:30:01Z
findings.why_not_priced: Announced after the close on the eve of the release, into a corpus with zero news-search coverage (n_queries=0 in every sweep) and a Stocktwits stream that had already moved on to other tickers - only two of six captured messages that evening even mention it. Sandwiching a compliance reverse split between a pivot acquisition and a results print is a disclosure sequence no aggregator assembles, and a compliance-driven reverse split is a statement that the company does not expect the market to lift the price on its own. If it were priced, the stock would not have been bid 25% higher two sessions earlier on a pivot headline.
findings.independence: A second, independent Stocktwits participant reads the same sequence the same way the same evening - 'merger and they hav to r/s and er tomorrow this all adds up to a big pile of shit salad' - docs/ee32750e276846aba37596bed7e3b23135338ee9.txt

findings.finding: Two sessions before the print, on 2026-08-31, CollPlant announced it was acquiring LightSolver and entering the photonic-computing and supercomputing markets - consideration paid in newly issued shares AND warrants - and the stock traded 182,733,300 shares against a float the corpus puts at 13.0-13.5m, halted up, ran roughly 35% intraday, and closed only 8.4% higher before giving it all back over the next two sessions.
findings.corpus_ref: snapshots/20260831T150738Z.json item 2 (6-K accession 0001213900-26-095458, accepted 2026-08-31T10:07:51Z); docs/5135d7c19b08a747e07fe6779eb96726eb106de8.txt; quote.json bars 2026-08-27 through 2026-09-02
findings.why_not_priced: The announcement is public, so the headline is priced; the unaggregated part is the shape of the flow. 182.7m shares against a 13m float is roughly fourteen turns of the entire float in one session with the close only 8.4% up and a full round-trip within two days - that is distribution into retail, not accumulation. Nothing in the corpus computes that ratio, and there is no sell-side coverage of this name at all. A regenerative-medicine issuer buying a photonic-computing company for paper, two days before releasing results, is the same reframing-before-bad-numbers pattern.
findings.independence: filings.json shows the issuance machinery that makes the paper consideration credible as dilution rather than as strategy: F-1 (2026-03-30), F-1/A, 424B3 (2026-04-21 and 2026-07-17), F-3 (2026-01-09 and 2026-07-09), 424B5 (2026-02-06) and two Form Ds (2026-02-17, 2026-07-20) - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1631487/000121390026095458/ea0303994-6k_collplant.htm

findings.finding: Three SCHEDULE 13D/A amendments were filed in twenty-five days - 2026-07-27, 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-21 - in a company whose float the corpus puts at 13.0-13.5m shares, immediately after a Form D private placement (2026-07-20) and a resale prospectus going effective (424B3, 2026-07-17).
findings.why_not_priced: 13D/A bodies are not stored and nothing in the capture references them. Three amendments in under a month at a sub-$50m issuer means a >5% holder's position is moving materially while a resale shelf is live - a supply fact with no publisher.
findings.independence: none - this rests on the same EDGAR index as finding 2 and should be collapsed into that source cluster.

searched_and_found_nothing: any confirmation from a company source that a results release is actually scheduled for 2026-09-03 - the baseline's own cadence check rejects the inferred event, and the capture directory is dated 2026-09-02
any news-wire or sell-side coverage: n_queries=0 in all six sweeps, so no consensus, no estimate, no analyst view of the LightSolver deal
the bodies of the two pre-print 6-Ks, the F-3, the 424B3 and the three 13D/As
any cash-runway or financing disclosure that would size the dilution
any Nasdaq deficiency letter or compliance correspondence beyond what the reverse-split release implies
baseline_tension: It cuts against the run-up, which is +11.4% over five sessions and +10.7% over twenty on the pivot headline, and it argues the historical 3.73% median magnitude is far too small for a name running 114.6% realised vol into a reverse split.
corpus_limits: No option chain, so no implied move or skew. No news search was run for this ticker; every non-filing item is Stocktwits, which for a sub-$1 momentum microcap is mostly promotional noise, and I discarded the pump content and used only the two dated announcements it reproduces. Note a data inconsistency I did not build on: the baseline reports a $3.43 spot while quote.json shows $0.31-0.39 closes for the same dates, which is Yahoo retro-adjusting for the 1-for-10 reverse split that the corpus says takes effect on 2026-09-04 - i.e. the baseline series is post-split-adjusted. I treated the split as a corpus-disclosed forward event (from the 2026-09-01 release) and not as an outcome. No item in this capture carried a non-empty tripwire_tells.
